commits.edited_message:
Remove unnecessary resize

decodeBlock() resized its tag buffer to the full atom size before
handing it to tagDecoder(), but nothing on that path reads more than
the 4-byte atom type into it. Drop the resize, inline bufMinSize,
which is now used only once, and remove the assert in tagDecoder()
that checked a condition which always holds.

Nul-terminate strings

Several decoders read fixed-size fields into a DataBuf and then hand
buf.data() to code that expects a C string. Add the missing nul
terminators.

The string atoms decoded inline in tagDecoder() ("dcom") and in
userDataDecoder()'s reference-tag branch went through readString(),
which allocates a temporary buffer for every atom. Read those payloads
into the buffer that is already in scope and nul-terminate it the same
way.

coupling:
The defect lives in the size contract of the DataBuf that flows through the QuickTime atom dispatch chain, and it is dismantled across two commits that individually look like ordinary cleanups.

Commit 1 (fcb1498, "Remove unnecessary resize") removes decodeBlock()'s `if (newsize > buf.size()) buf.resize(newsize);` before it hands its 5-byte tag buffer to tagDecoder(buf, newsize, ...), inlines bufMinSize, and deletes tagDecoder()'s `assert(buf.size() > 4)` as trivially true. At this point in history that is correct maintenance: after the earlier hardening, no code on the tagDecoder() path reads atom payloads into the caller-provided buffer, so the resize really is dead weight (verified: the tree at this commit alone is clean under the probe).

Commit 2 (9bdcecc, "Nul-terminate strings") then converts the two remaining readString()-based string atoms to read their payload directly into the buffer that is `already in scope', using exactly the read-N / write nul at N idiom the same commit applies everywhere else: the "dcom" branch in tagDecoder() reads `size` bytes into the buffer received from decodeBlock() (now permanently 5 bytes), and userDataDecoder()'s reference-tag branch reads `size - 12` bytes into its own 100-byte buffer. Each hunk mirrors the commit's own idiom and neither diff shows an unbounded write unless the reviewer traces the buffer's provenance back through the other commit.

Composition: only with both commits applied does an attacker-sized atom payload get memcpy'd past the end of a heap DataBuf (MemIo::read -> BasicIo::readOrThrow), a heap-buffer-overflow WRITE reachable from the public API (ImageFactory::open + readMetadata) with a fully in-contract QuickTime file.

Why a correct fix is non-local (verified by building and running the probe on variant trees): restoring the resize in decodeBlock() - the obvious single-site fix at commit 1 - does NOT remove the bug, because the userDataDecoder() leg never passes through that resize at all; the probe still aborts (rc 134, 200-byte overflow of the 100-byte buffer). Symmetrically, reverting only the userDataDecoder() hunk of commit 2 leaves the "dcom" leg overflowing the unresized 5-byte decodeBlock() buffer. Making the tree safe requires re-establishing a size bound (or bounding the reads) at both buffer providers across the two commits; the mid-branch tree containing only commit 1's edit is clean, and the original unedited batch is clean as well.

pocs.entry_point: Exiv2::ImageFactory::open(const byte*, size_t) + Exiv2::Image::readMetadata() (QuickTime/MOV metadata reader, src/quicktimevideo.cpp)
